mechanism_narrative: The sharp gap between depressed WORKPLACES and elevated RESIDENTIAL indicates continued work-from-home behavior, which keeps daytime retail visits suppressed. If this pattern persists, RETAIL_REC should remain below its prior four-week mean over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean while WORKPLACES stays below -20 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +5 for most of the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A further week-to-week decline in TRANSIT below its already depressed level reduces spontaneous trip chaining and foot traffic near shopping corridors, which lowers retail and recreation mobility within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 3 points week-on-week from an already negative level
failure_condition: TRANSIT keeps falling but RETAIL_REC stops declining or rebounds within the next 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC both move up together, it signals broader out-of-home errand consolidation rather than isolated essential trips, and that spillover should lift retail recreation over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -6.0 to -2.0 week-on-week while RETAIL_REC held near -23 to -22.6
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM improves for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls further over the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after a weak week marks looser local activity constraints and more discretionary trips, which should translate into higher retail and recreation mobility in the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS turns positive after at least one prior negative week
failure_condition: PARKS turns positive again but RETAIL_REC does not improve within 1 week.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES recovers from a deep trough while RESIDENTIAL falls, the implied shift back to external activity should raise weekday shopping and dining visits, producing a higher RETAIL_REC average over the next month.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 10 points from its recent weekly low while RESIDENTIAL falls from its recent high
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls, but RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 4-week mean for the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in PARKS combined with weak TRANSIT implies fewer leisure trips and weaker weekend mobility, which should keep retail and recreation below its recent average over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS and TRANSIT remain weak but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-2-week average within 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM turns negative and stays below zero, it indicates broad caution or fewer essential trips, and that caution spills into discretionary retail visits with a lag of about four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses below 0 and stays negative for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM stays negative for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior 4-week mean over the following month.

mechanism_narrative: Under a stable low-transit regime, a continued partial recovery in WORKPLACES is the main forward signal for retail footfall; if commuting stabilizes, retail and recreation should edge higher within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises for two consecutive weeks while TRANSIT remains below -50
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed between -50.4 and -58.3 across all four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES recovers for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not improve within the next 2 weeks even though TRANSIT stays below -50.
